## Historical audit: S0262

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task01/reference/H_start/test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Stage | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate editable meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, proportions, occlusions and materials. The inferred scene goal was a kitchen; that identification comes from the student’s inventory, not an image independently available to this audit (student request, line 1 [0,11547); student response, line 3 [0,12287)). |
| First build | The program defined multiple assets: room, floor, slats, door, bench, counter, sink, hob, backsplash, cabinets and extractor. Named child parts include the door handle and sink walls/rims. It configured procedural stone and wood materials, camera and lights. These definitions establish intended structure, not correct physical connections or visible coverage (student response, line 3 [0,12287); execute step 1, line 4 [0,12939)). |
| Validation and exploration | Step 1 returned `ok: true`, saved an image and blend file, and was selected. The next student request included the reference and rendered image and asked for comparison (execution result, line 5 [0,24419); select, line 6 [0,59); request, line 7 [0,48396)). The student independently reported that the door appeared too far right/down, perspective faced across the worktop, cabinets were too narrow/pale, and name-based material selection failed because primitives had generic names. These are student diagnoses, not independent visual verification (response, line 9 [0,13956)). |
| Revision and result | The student changed camera position/target, shifted and shortened the kitchen run, moved the sink, widened/darkened cabinets, changed lighting and exposure, and selected materials by geometric bounds. The complete revision was executed; step 2 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected (response, line 9 [0,13956); execute, line 10 [0,14608); result, line 11 [0,24174); select, line 12 [0,59)). |
| Teacher input | No teacher event, teacher diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or student receipt/adoption of one appears in this trajectory. The comparison prompt and feedback above are runner input and student assessment, respectively—not teacher intervention. The two student sessions record no tool calls (lines 2 [0,2877), 7 [0,48396), 8 [0,3356), 9 [0,13956)). |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Both builds formally executed and rendered successfully; step 2 was selected. Reconstruction correctness and whether the revision improved it remain **unknown**: neither image is visible in the supplied observations, and no final visual assessment or score is recorded. The code specifies multiple objects, surface textures, component placement, camera and lighting, but does not independently establish their visual fidelity, actual part contact, or absence of occlusion and render problems. No articulated pose is described; viewpoint is the relevant pose issue. The faucet and hidden/cropped geometry were explicitly uncertain (line 9 [0,13956)).

**Lessons.** Transferably, a rendered comparison can motivate separating framing, local geometry and material-assignment hypotheses, then testing a complete revision. Here, bounds-based material assignment and specific camera/cabinet changes are task-specific attempts, not proven fixes; the revised render would need independent inspection to resolve those hypotheses.
